563: Exhibitions for Cement Hranice, the Chocenice festival and Forestry Day
564: Split into 3 teams, we covered a large part of our beautiful country. Martin Šimůnek headed to Ralsko, where several tens of thousands of visitors gather at the mega event Forestry Day to check out the machinery and everything connected with the forest. It also includes a rich side programme, which traditionally includes an exhibition by Martin and our team.
565: {1}Michal Budský and Lukáš Valný, on the other hand, crossed the whole country to Hranice, where Cement Hranice was celebrating a respectable 70 years since its founding. It had one big advantage – the obstacles were already prepared on site, so the guys got to ride on concrete blocks and bags of cement.
566: {1}Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Mára Tryner went to Chocenice near Plzeň with our Kabeláč kids' selection, jumping at a small village festival. Everyone has a technical problem sometimes, and this time it was us – or rather Mára Tryner, whose chain tensioner spring snapped. Luckily a spring was found on Nikolka Kabeláčová's bike, and she took on the role of photographer. Judging by the feedback the event went great, and the beautiful weather helped bring in a big turnout.
568: We've prepared the dates of the events our team is planning for this year. Of course everything depends on the easing of current restrictions – camps and day camps will be possible with at least 10 riders / participants, or ideally the planned 20.
569: We know that big events like Říčanské Šlapačky are really up in the air, but smaller sports-focused events should have a better chance of success. Unfortunately we've had to cut back our plans for camps in Moravia, but we've added a few dates of classic one-day camps, which we'll expand with different levels and locations on the trails.
570: We once again want to pass on some of our knowledge of technical riding and the pump track to learning-hungry women – and, for 2021, to their male counterparts too.
571: Due to great success we're also planning kids' day camps focused on MTB and the pump track.
572: We'll publish the camp programme, prices and other details as soon as possible.
574: This year's first weekend with several events – there'll be more of those this year. On a rainy Saturday we held a slightly reduced Bikeskills camp for men, which had to be interrupted in the afternoon because the riders were soaked – even waterproof jackets couldn't take any more water. Sunday turned out much better, and a bigger group of women enjoyed the sunshine. We rode a few new spots in the area and the progress was very decent. Just before the end of the camp, Vlasta, the only male disturbing element, broke away and set off with Lukáš Valný and Matouš Balík for a big event by the Miskovice lookout tower.
575: More than a thousand people came to celebrate witch-burning night, enjoy the competitions and concerts and check out our team's new obstacle setup. Thanks for the cooperation, and to Aleš Matoušek for co-hosting and DJing the whole event.
578: Vlasta rode an exhibition for the cycling and leisure shop Harfa Sport in cooperation with Levelsportkoncept (our team partner). Thanks to that he got to try out a loaned Superior bike, which he then used to ride down and up the stairs in the shop, as well as for a bit of hopping on the obstacles, to show that XC bikes from Superior can take something too. Since time for practice on the bike was limited and he hadn't ridden it in, for the jumps over volunteers he reached for his Trial bike. Among the guests, Olympian Ondřej Synek lay down under Vlasta. Visitors could see the new collections of clothing, accessories and bikes for the coming bike season.
579: End of the summer holidays on the road
580: The end of the holidays was a bit hectic. We got to visit a few interesting festivals and town celebrations and coached several enthusiastic male and female bikers.
581: Martin Šimůnek worked with Míra Brunclík at the village festival in Kvítkov and couldn't praise the local audience enough – after all, it was practically on their doorstep.
582: Vlasta, Tobík Dolák and Lukáš Valný, on the other hand, went to a festival in Kaplice, where unfortunately there was a bit of organisational noise. Simply put, plans work until they don't, and here it didn't work out. Anyway, after agreeing with the event organisers, a slot was found between bands where we could perform. To our credit, we drew the biggest crowd in front of the main stage of the whole afternoon.
583: On the last day of the summer holidays Vlasta, Nikolka Kabeláčová and moto-trial rider Dalibor Šulc headed to the beer festival in Jevišovice, where in 33 degrees they rode a 40-minute exhibition followed by a workshop in the beautiful smallest town in South Moravia. It has to be said they have a really beautiful historic centre. We also coped with sloping terrain and made good use of our team sound system, since we operated as an independent unit. Thanks to everyone for the invitations – we look forward to the September events.
585: As the article published in Říčansko suggests, we're now looking into building trails around Říčany, which would free up forest paths for walkers and slightly discourage the building of some illegal trails – because why do something illegally when it could be done together and legally?
586: Moreover, when it comes to trails, Říčany – a town that lives for cycling – is missing something like this. The route study was prepared by Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, and it looks like recreational riders could enjoy it, as well as – thanks to smaller side lines – those who can ride.
587: Javornicko Days, Forestry Day, Solfest, Sokolov, Prague 15, a Trial course and a natural disaster
588: This week was one of the most demanding I can imagine as a rider and organiser. Thursday started with a morning Trial course for guys who want to fulfil their biker dream and peek behind the scenes of Trial. In the afternoon we headed to Prague 15, where a kids' pump track was being opened with the city leadership in attendance, and my son Márty and I rode a father-and-son exhibition there. On Saturday our team split into 3: Michal Budský and Tobík Dolák rode Forestry Day in Ralsko, Martin Šimůnek and Dominik Budský did an exhibition and workshop in Sokolov, and Lukáš Valný and I went to Javornicko Days, where we rode just before Imagine Diamonds. We finished riding and practically right after us it started raining. Unfortunately, when we got home we found out that a windstorm had swept through the Říčany area and Tehov and flooded our houses/gardens. The parks we manage were hit too, so what followed was dealing with our caretaker duties. On Sunday Martin Šimůnek, Vlasta and Lukáš Valný headed to Solnice for the local Solfest festival, where in incredible heat they rode an exhibition and handed out a few drinks. After returning, more dealing with the aftermath of the windstorm – and that awaits us all next week too.
589: Camps for women and men no. 1
590: Excellent weather and turnout, a relaxed atmosphere and the desire to improve were the cornerstones of our camps. All participants tried not only to take in everything we wanted to pass on but also to overcome their fear. Of course, all with regard to the participants' bikes and their current abilities. The progress by the end of the camp was more than visible, and every single rider deserves praise. In the men's camp we made an exception and took on one mini guy with his dad, who was backed up by our team mascot Marty Kabeláč.
591: Vchynice village festival and individual courses
592: The start of the summer holidays was mainly about individual courses for older enduro riders and young guns, which Vlasta took charge of. On Saturday he and Martin Šimůnek with a bunch of kids went training in Šimi's stomping ground (the beaches of Lake Mácha), where they crushed Martin's traditional spots, and then set off for the village of Vchynice, to the newly renovated village barn, which the locals have turned into a community centre.
593: A beautiful place and luxurious weather were ideal for an exhibition of more than 30 minutes, where both the kids and Vlasta with Martin performed for the locals. We managed a few competitions, drops off the trailer, a jump onto a car and jumps over volunteers, and after the exhibition the kids could catch sweets falling on ribbons from a plane.
595: We were supposed to ride the exhibition in Rohozná before Covid, but unfortunately you can't control an epidemic and the event was postponed several times. Before the exhibition itself we visited the Trial park in Hamry nad Sázavou, where we did a light training session that within an hour turned into cold, cloudy, windy weather. We'd given it our all, so there was no point risking injury and we set off for Rohozná.
596: This village of 300–400 inhabitants evidently knows how to have fun, and they'd prepared a pretty nice programme with the facilities of the local football club, which was playing its match when we arrived.
597: When we arrived the weather still looked good, but unfortunately the tradition of the last 3 weeks repeated itself, and Vlasta and Lukáš Valný with little Marty Kabeláč waited in the car for the rain to stop. After an hour it was clear it wasn't going to pass, and the spectators wanted to be entertained. And since the guys were the highlight of the programme, there was nothing left but to pluck up courage and try to show some Trial art even in the rain. Luckily it all went without a big crash, even though the grass and our obstacles were slippery as ice.
598: The spectators were great and praised the whole team for both the performance and the attitude. We look forward to Rohozná again in 2023.
600: At a day's notice we were asked for an exhibition at the traditional Nursery School Olympics in Prague, hosted by the school and nursery in Měcholupy. The organisation was in the hands of Radek Zavřel from the Czech Olympic Committee, so we knew what we were getting into. Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček took on the show, and since the event was for nurseries, he also brought his youngest rider Marty Kabeláč (with a proper excuse note for nursery, of course).
601: The kids gave it their all, and after their performance Vlasta and Márty showed them a bit of Trial art on the trailer and obstacles. Vlasta rode on top of them, Márty rode under them, and the teachers wanted to take Márty into their class straight away :)

626: A bikers' ball always gets wild, and because we know that, this year's first exhibition was ridden by the two chief wild ones, Martin Šimůnek and Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček.
627: The journey to Sosnová was a bit of a lottery with freshly fallen snow, but the warm welcome on site and a hall packed to the brim fired the guys up for an almost 30-minute show for the motorbike survivors of last season. Martin complained about a sore back, but he still put on an incredible hosted show that hopefully pleased every lover of handlebars.
